section_summary: This section closes a Japanese propaganda pamphlet defending Japan’s trade policy, anti-Communism, and Anti-Comintern alignment. It then contains two State Department file notes and a June 1939 despatch transmitting an issue of Brasil-Japão, a Japanese-supported cultural propaganda magazine published in Rio de Janeiro. The magazine promotes Brazilian–Japanese friendship, immigration, commerce, cultural exchange, Japanese industrial development, Manchukuo, and favorable portrayals of Japan and Brazil’s Estado Novo.

subfiles.title: Japanese propaganda pamphlet, concluding questions 46–50
subfiles.from: Japan Pacific Association; published by S. Nakado
subfiles.about: The concluding pages defend Japanese trade expansion, dependence on imported raw materials, policy in China, anti-Communism, and participation in the Anti-Comintern Pact.
subfiles.summary: Questions 46–48 argue that foreign tariffs obstruct Japanese exports even though Japan must sell manufactured goods to obtain raw materials, and that a stable, Japan-friendly China would benefit international commerce. Questions 49–50 portray Communism and the Soviet Union as existential threats while denying that Japan’s agreements with Germany and Italy constitute a fascist bloc. The final page supplies a Tokyo publication address and identifies a photograph of Suzhou dated January 1938.

subfiles.title: Document file note on Japanese activities in Brazil
subfiles.about: The note summarizes a report on Japanese efforts to secure immigration quotas and cultivate Brazilian military leaders.
subfiles.summary: File note: Japanese activity in Brazil aimed at larger immigration quotas, funded by the Embassy; the attache gave samurai swords to Brazil's war minister and chief of staff.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 1074
subfiles.about: The sheet cross-references a report on Japanese activities in Brazil during September 1938.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Brazil Despatch No. 1074 (December 19, 1938) on Japanese activities in Brazil in September 1938.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1379 transmitting Brasil-Japão
subfiles.from: William C. Burdett, Counselor of Embassy, for the U.S. Ambassador in Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: The U.S. Embassy transmitted a copy of Brasil-Japão as an example of Japanese-supported propaganda in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Burdett forwards 'Brasil-Japao', sponsored by the Brazilian Institute of Japanese Culture, which receives Japanese Embassy funds.

subfiles.title: Brasil-Japão, Year I, No. 2
subfiles.from: Instituto Brasileiro de Cultura Japoneza; Alexandre Konder, editor
subfiles.about: This illustrated Portuguese-language magazine promotes Japanese–Brazilian political, cultural, commercial, and migratory ties through laudatory articles about both countries.
subfiles.summary: The issue opens with its editorial staff, institute membership, contents, and a long tribute to President Getúlio Vargas and the Estado Novo, including immigration policy and military reform. Subsequent articles praise Japan, Manchukuo, Japanese industry, Noh theatre, Zen Buddhism, Japanese immigrants in Brazil, radio broadcasts, diplomatic exchanges, and new Japanese–Latin American cultural associations. It reproduces speeches and reports concerning Ambassadors Kazue Kuwajima and Frederico de Castello Branco Clark, and includes historical material on Portuguese contact with Japan. The surviving section ends during an article on the nutritional and chemical properties of yerba mate.
